clauses.requirement: Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (UN R48 para 6.16.1, Presence): shall be fitted where mandatory, i.e. mandatory on trailers and on motor vehicles having all forward facing lamps with reflectors concealable; optional on other motor vehicles.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (Number): two shall be fitted, type-approved as Class IA or IB retro-reflectors under the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 3, or the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 150; additional retro-reflecting devices and materials (including two retro-reflectors not complying with paragraph 6.16.4) are permitted provided they do not impair the effectiveness of the mandatory lighting and light-signalling devices.
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular (Arrangement): no special requirement applies to the arrangement.
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular: the position shall comply with the width, height and length requirements of paragraph 6.16.4 (6.16.4.1 to 6.16.4.3).

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in width: the point of the illuminating surface farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall be not more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle; for a trailer, not farther than 150 mm from the extreme outer edge; the distance between the inner edges of the two apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axes shall have no special requirement for M1 and N1 vehicles, and for all other categories be not less than 600 mm, which may be reduced to 400 mm where the overall vehicle width is less than 1,300 mm.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in height: above the ground, not less than 250 mm and not more than 900 mm (1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm).
Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, position in length: it shall be located at the front of the vehicle.

Front retro-reflector, non-triangular, geometric visibility: horizontal angle 30° inwards and outwards (for trailers the inward angle may be reduced to 10°; if trailer construction prevents the mandatory retro-reflectors meeting this angle, additional supplementary retro-reflectors shall be fitted, without the width limitation of 6.16.4.1, which together with the mandatory ones give the necessary visibility angle); vertical angle 10° above and below the horizontal, where the downward angle may be reduced to 5° if the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured per paragraph 5.8.1).
